_strings.@@07cde786876b: Treaty conformity — NE conforms to federal treaty treatment — income exempt from federal tax under a treaty is also excluded from NE income (it flows through the federal starting point; do not add it back on the NE return). (This is about TREATY conformity only — a state can conform on treaties while DECOUPLING from the federal Code for deductions or credits; see any law-change lines below.) State note: Nebraska's resident return (Form 1040N) starts from federal adjusted gross income: line 5 instructs "Enter the amount from Federal Form 1040 or 1040-SR, page 1, line 11." Federally treaty-exempt income is already excluded from federal AGI and therefore flows through. The only additions to federal AGI are on Nebraska Schedule I, Part A ("Adjustments Increasing Federal AGI"), whose nine line items are: (1) interest income from state/local obligations exempt from federal tax, (2) exempt interest from Nebraska obligations, (3) total taxable interest (line 1 minus line 2), (4) Financial Institution Tax Credit claimed, (5) Nebraska College Savings Program recapture, (6) Nebraska Enable plan recapture, (7) federal net operating loss deduction, (8) S corporation or LLC Non-Nebraska loss, and (9) Nebraska PTET deducted under IRC sec. 164. NONE of these requires adding back income exempt under a U.S. income tax treaty. With no treaty add-back and a federal-AGI starting point, treaty-exempt income is not re-taxed -> Nebraska conforms.
_strings.@@1b01fb3d7bf9: Form 1040N with Nebraska Schedule III (Computation of Nebraska Tax for Nonresidents and Partial-Year Residents); there is no separate nonresident form number — nonresidents and partial-year residents file the same Form 1040N and must attach Schedule III.

_strings.@@24bb929482c3: Nebraska Child/Dependent Care Credit (refundable, AGI $29,000 or less) — Full-year and partial-year residents whose federal AGI (Form 1040N, line 5) is $29,000 or less and who have qualifying federal child & dependent care expenses. Must complete and attach Nebraska Form 2441N (the federal Form 2441 alone is not accepted). Taxpayers who file federal MFJ but Nebraska MFS cannot claim it; nonresidents cannot claim it.

Must include a copy of federal Form 2441 (credit disallowed if not received). Taxpayers who file federal MFJ but Nebraska MFS cannot claim it; nonresidents cannot claim it (partial-year residents use Schedule III line 6c).

Nonresidents may not claim it. If filing Nebraska married-filing-separately, eligibility depends on whether the federal EIC is allowed on a federal MFS return.

state_tax.work_common_tail: . Tax line: Form 1040N, line 15 "Nebraska income tax" — the 2023 Tax Calculation Schedule states: "This calculation represents Nebraska income tax before any credits are applied. Enter on line 15, Form 1040N." Form 1040N line 15 text: "Nebraska income tax (Partial-year residents and nonresidents enter the result from line 9, Nebraska Schedule III. Paper filers may use the Nebraska Tax Table. All others must use Tax Calculation Schedule.)" This op computes the state's rate-schedule tax line ONLY — county/city add-on taxes, state credits, and any amounts outside the rate schedule are NOT modeled. Pack notes: Base guidance: Supply Form 1040N line 5 — federal adjusted gross income, i.e. Federal Form 1040 or 1040-SR, line 11. The pack ships Nebraska's standard deduction for the op to subtract, which reproduces line 14 (Nebraska Taxable Income = line 5 minus line 10 deduction, plus line 12 minus line 13 Schedule I adjustments) whenever there are no Nebraska Schedule I adjustments and the standard deduction is used. If Nebraska Schedule I adjustments apply, supply line 5 plus line 12 minus line 13 instead, so that subtracting the shipped standard deduction still reproduces line 14. Adjudication note (two-pass): vector counts are zero by design — Nebraska personal exemptions are a $157-per-person nonrefundable CREDIT on Form 1040N line 18, never an income exemption, so the pack ships no personal/dependent keys and the engine refuses nonzero counts. Nebraska personal exemptions are a TAX CREDIT, not an income exemption: Form 1040N line 18 gives RESIDENTS a nonrefundable credit of $157 times the number of Nebraska personal exemptions on line 4 (yourself, spouse, and dependents). It is subtracted from tax, not from income, so no personal/dependent amounts are shipped in exemptions and calc.state_tax does not apply it — claim it on line 18 of the form (nonresidents and partial-year residents claim it prorated on Nebraska Schedule III, line 7). The shipped standard deduction is the 2023 chart amount with ZERO boxes checked on Form 1040N line 2a (under 65, not blind) for a filer who cannot be claimed as a dependent. Nebraska Standard Deduction Chart (booklet p.9) with line-2a boxes checked: Single $9,750 (1 box) / $11,600 (2); Married Filing Jointly $17,300 / $18,800 / $20,300 / $21,800 (1-4 boxes); Qualifying surviving spouse $17,300 / $18,800 (1-2); Married Filing Separately $9,400 / $10,900 / $12,400 / $13,900 (1-4; the spouse's 65-and-over and blind boxes count only if the primary taxpayer can claim a personal exemption for the spouse); Head of Household $13,450 / $15,300 (1-2). These are NOT applied by calc.state_tax — use the chart amount on line 6. If you or your spouse CAN be claimed as a dependent by another taxpayer (Form 1040N line 2b), your standard deduction is the SMALLER of the federal standard deduction allowed on line 12 of Federal Form 1040/1040-SR or the Nebraska chart amount — not modeled; compute on the form. Itemizers are not modeled: taxpayers who itemized on the federal return take the LARGER of the Nebraska standard deduction or Nebraska itemized deductions (line 9 = federal Schedule A line 17 total minus line 5a state and local income taxes); if you used the federal standard deduction you MUST use the Nebraska standard deduction (booklet p.9, Line 6). Nebraska Schedule I adjustments (Form 1040N line 12 adjustments increasing federal AGI, line 13 adjustments decreasing federal AGI) are not modeled — if they apply, fold them into the supplied base per base_guidance or compute line 14 on the form. Tax table option (paper filers only): "Only taxpayers filing paper returns may use the Nebraska Tax Table" (booklet p.38); electronic filers must use the Tax Calculation Schedule (booklet p.10, Line 15), which is the exact bracket math this op implements. The table "calculates tax to the midpoint of the bracket" ($100-wide bands were observed) and covers Nebraska taxable income up to $71,560, so a paper filer's table amount may differ by a few dollars from this op's result within a band; above $71,560 the booklet worksheet is (taxable income - $71,560) x .0664 plus $3,798 Single/MFS, $2,844 MFJ/QSS, or $3,283 HoH. Qualifying surviving spouse: the schedule's second table is titled "Married Taxpayers, Filing Jointly and Qualifying Surviving Spouses" — the engine's QSS-to-MFJ mapping is exact for the brackets, and the QSS standard deduction with zero boxes is the same $15,800. Married filing separately is printed with the SAME schedule as Single on the 2023 Tax Calculation Schedule (identical breakpoints $3,700/$22,170/$35,730 and constants) — copied from the MFS table, not derived. The schedule's printed '$X + Y% of excess over $Z' constants are the exact cumulative bracket sums rounded to the nearest cent; maximum divergence from the exact sum is $0.007 (Single/MFS top constant $1,418.68 vs exact $1,418.673; also $739.32 vs $739.317; MFJ $181.79 vs $181.794 and $2,837.30 vs $2,837.301; HoH $1,172.90 vs $1,172.898 and $2,049.65 vs $2,049.648) — after rounding to whole dollars the results agree. Nebraska other tax is NOT modeled: Form 1040N line 16 adds 29.6% (x .296) of federal tax on lump-sum distributions of qualified retirement plans (Federal Form 4972) and federal tax on early distributions (lesser of Federal Form 5329 or Schedule 2 line 8); line 17 total tax = line 15 + line 16. Nonresidents and partial-year residents are NOT modeled: they compute line 15 via Nebraska Schedule III (line 9), which apportions the tax by the Nebraska-income ratio.
